title: Design Thinking for Startup: Transforming the thinking process to create products that meet real users' needs
image1Description: Workshop on the Design Thinking process with expert speakers in the Startup industry

section1.heading: Origin and Intent
section1.content: Creating successful software does not start with beautiful Code, but starts from a deep 'understanding of the problem' of the users. I joined the Design Thinking training to learn systematic thinking principles for Software Startup development. My goal was to use this process to Validate my ideas to see if they can truly answer business needs and solve Pain Points for users before starting development.

section2.heading: Role and Action
section2.content: I practiced the full Design Thinking process, from Empathize to understand the problem, Define to specify key issues, to Ideate to brainstorm creative solutions. I brought my own Startup project ideas to analyze weaknesses through the perspective of experienced speakers to find ways to improve and identify necessary information for further research, ensuring the Product's foundation is strong enough to compete in the market.

section3.heading: Challenges
section3.content: The most important challenge was to 'Unlearn' old beliefs and confidence in my first ideas to open up to new information from User Research. Having the courage to accept that some ideas might Not Work and being ready to Pivot according to Design Thinking principles was a mental test that helped me clearly see blind spots and gaps I had overlooked.

section4.heading: Results and Learning
section4.content: This training gave me a valuable 'compass' for product development. I gained an understanding that a great product is the intersection of user Desirability, technical Feasibility, and business Viability. This experience not only developed my creative thinking skills but also allowed me to design a Framework for developing other products in the future systematically and reduce the risk of wasted investment.
